title: Dietary Reference Values for choline
authors: EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition and Allergies (NDA)
funder: European Food Safety Authority; requestor: European Commission (question number EFSA-Q-2011-01208).
result: For all adults the Panel set an Adequate Intake of 400 mg choline per day, with 480 mg in pregnancy and 520 mg in lactation; Average Requirements could not be derived. Dietary phosphatidylcholine, glycerophosphocholine and sphingomyelin are hydrolysed by phospholipases to liberate choline. Choline is an integral part of some phospholipids, a precursor of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine and of betaine, to which it is irreversibly oxidised in liver and kidney; betaine is the methyl-group donor in the betaine-homocysteine methyltransferase (BHMT) reaction, which converts homocysteine to methionine. Dietary choline deficiency can cause fatty liver and liver and muscle damage. Total choline content is highest in eggs.
